N-Deklination: German B1 Exercises with Answers

Study four German examples with English meanings, then try four questions and check the explained answers.

B1 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the rule

Certain masculine nouns take -n or -en outside Nominativ singular: der Student → den Studenten → dem Studenten → des Studenten. Common examples include Student, Kollege, Junge and Mensch.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not add the extra -n to ordinary masculine nouns such as der Tisch.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Ich sehe den Studenten.I see the student.
Worked example 2Wir helfen dem Kollegen.We help the colleague.
Worked example 3Das Spielzeug gehört dem Jungen.The toy belongs to the boy.
Worked example 4Er kennt diesen Menschen.He knows this person.

Practice: fill in the gaps

Put the noun in brackets into the case required by the sentence. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Ich treffe den ___. (Student)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: Studenten

Akkusativ singular N-declension.

Question 2. Sie spricht mit dem ___. (Kollege)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: Kollegen

Dativ singular N-declension.

Question 3. Das Geschenk ist für den ___. (Junge)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: Jungen

Akkusativ singular N-declension.

Question 4. Das ist das Auto des ___. (Mensch)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: Menschen

Genitiv singular N-declension.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
